top.title: Scaling agentic AI with data transformations
top.summary: McKinsey research shows that fewer than 10% of enterprises have scaled AI agents to deliver tangible value, with 80% citing data limitations as the primary roadblock. The article outlines foundational requirements: unified data definitions, consolidated data platforms, embedded governance, stable APIs, and continuous performance measurement.
top.relevance: Critical for consulting leaders advising on enterprise AI scaling; data quality and architecture are the decisive competitive factors, not model sophistication.

top.title: AI at Work: Why Strategy Matters More Than Tools
top.summary: BCG survey of 12,000 employees finds 74% of frontline workers now use AI daily or several times weekly, yet only 42% of organizations have graduated to reshaping workflows end-to-end. Strategic clarity and explicit transformation plans correlate strongly with measurable business impact.
top.relevance: Demonstrates the gap between AI adoption and actual value capture; organizations must redesign operations and workforce strategies, not just deploy tools.

top.title: Agents think in milliseconds, legacy infrastructure doesn't
top.summary: VentureBeat panel with LinkedIn, Walmart, and Zendesk infrastructure leaders reveals that legacy systems and data pipelines, not AI models, are the bottleneck slowing agent deployment. Organizations must modernize data architecture and APIs to unlock agent velocity.
top.relevance: Shifts focus from model selection to infrastructure modernization as the real competitive battleground; consulting leaders should prioritize systems architecture and data platform upgrades.

top.title: The agent security gap: 54% of enterprises have already had an AI agent incident
top.summary: VentureBeat survey of 107 enterprises reveals 54% have experienced an AI agent security incident or near-miss; only about one-third assign scoped identity to each agent, and most allow credential sharing. The gap between agent deployment speed and security controls is widening.
top.relevance: Critical risk area for enterprise deployments; consulting practices must integrate security governance frameworks into AI agent strategies before large-scale rollouts.

top.title: The AI compute gap: Enterprises are buying infrastructure faster than they can measure what it costs
top.summary: VentureBeat survey of 107 enterprises finds AI infrastructure spending is accelerating while visibility and steering of AI economics remains poor. Organizations lack mechanisms to track compute costs across hyperscalers, specialized hardware, and API providers, creating financial governance gaps.
top.relevance: Reveals a major unmet need in AI cost management and FinOps; consulting leaders can capitalize by building AI spend governance and optimization practices for clients deploying at scale.

top.title: Four Ways to Accelerate Growth with AI and Analytics
top.summary: BCG article outlines four growth levers: using agentic AI for real-time strategy alerts, mining customer data for emerging needs, applying analytics to competitive intelligence, and using AI for dynamic pricing and personalization. Companies leveraging these capabilities gain competitive advantage.
top.relevance: Positions analytics and AI as strategic weapons for growth, not just cost reduction; aligns with evolving consulting narratives around value creation and business model transformation.

top.title: Private Equity's Future: Digital First and AI Powered
top.summary: BCG outlines the PE playbook for integrating digital and AI into portfolio companies: establish ERP/CRM as foundational data layers from day one, launch 100-day digital sprints post-acquisition, sequence initiatives to build data governance and integration capabilities before advanced AI. Winners treat digital as integral to value creation, not a separate stream.
top.relevance: Provides consulting leaders with a replicable playbook for embedding analytics and AI into operating model transformations; emphasizes sequencing and data governance as critical success factors.

top.title: BCG AI Radar 2026: As AI Investments Surge, CEOs Take the Lead
top.summary: Nearly 75% of CEOs are their company's chief AI decision maker and remain bullish on investments, yet over 50% believe their job stability depends on AI strategy success. Agentic AI represents a growing share of AI budgets as organizations move from experimentation to deployment.
top.relevance: Highlights the strategic urgency and C-suite stakes around AI; consulting leaders should position AI governance and ROI measurement as business-critical, not IT-only concerns.

top.title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
top.summary: Survey of nearly 2,000 respondents across 105 countries shows that while almost all organizations use AI, high performers allocate >20% of digital budgets to AI, maintain robust data governance, embed AI into business processes, and track KPIs systematically. Leadership commitment and agile delivery models are key differentiators.
top.relevance: Establishes benchmarks for high-performing organizations; provides data-driven framework for consulting engagements on AI maturity and value realization.

top.title: Intelligence at scale: Data monetization in the age of gen AI
top.summary: McKinsey research shows one-third of executives believe their data assets remain undermonetized. As synthetic data erodes raw data pricing and regulatory scrutiny tightens, successful data monetization requires moving beyond data brokerage to analytics-as-a-service and AI-powered customer insights. Proprietary advantage and domain expertise become differentiators.
top.relevance: Reframes data strategy for the AI era; consulting leaders should help clients transition from commodity data plays to contextualized intelligence products leveraging proprietary domain knowledge.

ai.title: Enterprise AI agents crossed from pilot to production in 2026
ai.summary: Comprehensive statistics from Gartner, McKinsey, and IDC show agentic AI market reaching $10.9-12.1 billion (2026), 40% of enterprise applications embedding agents by year-end (up from under 5% in 2025), with 3.7x average ROI but 40% project cancellation rates cited by Gartner due to governance gaps.
ai.relevance: Current market sizing, adoption velocity, and project failure rates provide essential context for portfolio prioritization, governance investment decisions, and competitive positioning in analytics modernization.

ai.title: A scorecard for the AI age
ai.summary: OpenAI CFO introduces practical AI scorecard measuring ROI through useful work, cost per successful task, dependability, and return on compute—a metrics framework designed to move beyond hype and focus on measurable business outcomes.
ai.relevance: Essential measurement framework for analytics teams designing AI performance dashboards, cost attribution models, and business case validation for enterprise AI agent projects.

ai.title: How to manage AI investments in the agentic era
ai.summary: OpenAI guidance on measuring useful work per dollar, improving efficiency, and scaling high-value workflows as the financial discipline framework for managing AI investments during the agentic transition.
ai.relevance: Practical framework for analytics and finance leaders to establish ROI metrics, cost controls, and workflow prioritization aligned with enterprise value realization from AI agent deployments.

ai.title: Deutsche Telekom is rewiring telecommunications with AI
ai.summary: Deutsche Telekom case study demonstrates large-scale agentic AI deployment transforming customer service, employee workflows, network operations, and voice interaction at a Fortune 500 telco with integrated governance and change management.
ai.relevance: Real-world example of enterprise-wide agentic AI adoption in operations and analytics-heavy environment, illustrating governance, integration, and workflow redesign patterns applicable to complex organizations.

ai.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
ai.summary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.6 frontier model with stronger performance per dollar and increased capability on demand, integrated into ChatGPT Work and Microsoft 365 Copilot, addressing cost-performance tradeoffs critical for enterprise deployment.
ai.relevance: Latest frontier model capabilities and pricing structure inform strategic decisions on model selection, cost management, and analytics workflow automation in enterprise AI stacks.

ai.title: State of AI in the Enterprise - 2026 AI report
ai.summary: Deloitte's 2026 survey of 3,235 leaders documents worker AI access rising 50% in 2025 and companies with 40% of AI projects in production doubling within six months, though only one in five has mature agentic AI governance and the skills gap remains the primary adoption barrier.
ai.relevance: Addresses talent, governance, and production deployment readiness—critical for analytics teams planning organizational capability building and risk management frameworks as AI moves from pilot to scale.

ai.title: How agents are transforming work
ai.summary: OpenAI research paper demonstrates how AI agents enable longer, more complex tasks and expand productivity across roles by orchestrating multi-step workflows autonomously, with practical applications across knowledge work and operational domains.
ai.relevance: Provides evidence-based perspective on agentic workflow transformation applicable to analytics and decision support roles, directly relevant to planning analytics platform modernization and agent-ready data architectures.

ai.title: Reimagining tech infrastructure for agentic AI
ai.summary: McKinsey outlines how IT infrastructure must evolve to support agentic AI workloads, with domain-specific agents orchestrated through multi-layer architectures and projected infrastructure costs increasing two to three times by 2030 despite flat budgets.
ai.relevance: Critical for data leaders planning infrastructure modernization and cost management strategies needed to support autonomous analytics and agent-powered decision workflows at enterprise scale.

ai.title: State of AI trust in 2026: Shifting to the agentic era
ai.summary: McKinsey's 2026 AI Trust Maturity Survey reveals that while RAI maturity improved to 2.3 (up from 2.0 in 2025), only one-third of organizations reach maturity level three or higher in strategy and agentic AI governance, indicating critical gaps between adoption acceleration and risk management capability.
ai.relevance: Directly addresses enterprise governance, risk, and organizational alignment challenges that constrain agentic AI scaling—essential intelligence for planning analytics governance and AI risk frameworks.

ai.title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
ai.summary: McKinsey's survey of 1,993 respondents shows 88% of organizations use AI in at least one function, but only 23% are scaling agentic AI and just 39% report enterprise-level EBIT impact, revealing a significant gap between experimentation and value capture.
ai.relevance: Provides benchmark data on agentic AI adoption maturity, ROI realization, and high-performer patterns—essential context for setting realistic expectations and identifying best practices in AI investment management.

platforms.title: Databricks Hits $188B Valuation, Extending Its Run as AI's Favorite Second Act
platforms.summary: TechCrunch analysis of the Databricks $188B funding round frames the company's transformation from a data engineering vendor into a full AI platform, noting its open-weight model research and cost-savings narrative. Sacra estimates Databricks reached approximately $6.9B in annualized revenue in June 2026, growing roughly 80% year-over-year in Q2 2026.
platforms.relevance: Third-party analysis of Databricks' AI repositioning and accelerating revenue growth is essential context for advisory teams helping clients assess build-versus-buy decisions on agentic AI data infrastructure.

platforms.title: Databricks is Raising a Strategic Round of Funding at a $188 Billion Valuation
platforms.summary: Databricks announced a new strategic funding round at a $188 billion valuation, led by existing investor Coatue and expected to close later in summer 2026. New capital will accelerate Unity AI Gateway for multi-AI governance, Genie AI coworker, and Lakebase serverless Postgres database.
platforms.relevance: The rapid valuation step-up from $134B to $188B in under a year signals that enterprise AI data platform infrastructure remains a top investment priority; clients evaluating Databricks for long-term platform bets should factor in its deepening AI product roadmap and likely 2027 IPO trajectory.

platforms.title: The Open Interoperability Standard: Why Bidirectional Iceberg REST Matters
platforms.summary: Snowflake published a detailed technical and strategic argument for bidirectional Apache Iceberg REST Catalog interoperability, contrasting its Snowflake Horizon implementation against Databricks Unity Catalog's inbound-only approach. The post frames true data portability as requiring full bidirectional federation, not just read access.
platforms.relevance: The Snowflake-Databricks interoperability debate directly affects multiplatform data architecture recommendations; consulting leaders need to understand the competing governance and portability claims as clients increasingly run workloads across both platforms.

platforms.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Now in Private Preview on Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.summary: Snowflake announced that OpenAI's GPT-5.6, described as OpenAI's most capable model, is now available in private preview on Snowflake Cortex AI, enabling access to the latest frontier model within Snowflake's secure, governed platform. This follows the broader $200 million OpenAI partnership announced in February 2026.
platforms.relevance: Access to the latest frontier model inside a governed data perimeter accelerates enterprise AI agent development timelines and is a concrete differentiator to highlight when advising clients on Cortex AI versus self-managed LLM integration approaches.

platforms.title: Snowflake Marketplace Partners Earn $100M in the First Half of 2026
platforms.summary: Snowflake reported that Marketplace partners earned over $100 million in revenue in H1 2026, representing 277% year-over-year growth, driven by expansion of AI agents, Snowflake Native Apps, and AI-ready data offerings. The milestone signals the platform's growing role as a commercial distribution channel for enterprise AI products.
platforms.relevance: The 277% partner revenue growth rate reveals that Snowflake's ecosystem flywheel is accelerating alongside its AI platform investments, a key data point for clients assessing the long-term commercial and partner landscape on Snowflake versus competing platforms.

platforms.title: Build 2026: From Data to Intelligence — Faster with Fabric Data Factory
platforms.summary: Microsoft Build 2026 featured a broad wave of Fabric Data Factory enhancements including private-link mirroring for Azure SQL, SAP Datasphere, and SharePoint; native dbt integration inside Dataflow Gen2; and expanded AI-assisted Airflow authoring. These updates position Fabric Data Factory as the enterprise integration backbone for AI application pipelines.
platforms.relevance: The depth of Build 2026 Fabric Data Factory releases — particularly native dbt support and private-network mirroring for SAP — lowers the migration friction for complex enterprise estates and strengthens the case for Fabric as a credible alternative to multi-tool data integration stacks.

platforms.title: FabCon and SQLCon 2026: Unifying Databases and Fabric on a Single Data Platform
platforms.summary: At FabCon and SQLCon 2026 in Atlanta, Microsoft announced the convergence of SQL Server and Microsoft Fabric into a single unified data platform, introduced Fabric data agents now generally available, and highlighted that Fabric now serves over 31,000 customers as the fastest-growing data platform in Microsoft history. Fabric IQ and Power BI's semantic model technology were featured as the layer connecting data to AI understanding.
platforms.relevance: Fabric's GA of data agents and its convergence with SQL Server represent a significant architectural consolidation that consulting leaders must factor into client roadmaps, particularly for Microsoft-centric enterprises evaluating migration away from Synapse or standalone Azure services.

platforms.title: Snowflake Q4 FY 2026 Results Highlight AI-Led Consumption and Platform Expansion
platforms.summary: Futurum analyst review of Snowflake's Q4 FY2026 results finds that Q4 product revenue grew 30% year-over-year to $1.23 billion, with over 9,100 customer accounts using AI capabilities and Snowflake Intelligence scaling to 2,500 accounts in under three months. The company posted a 61% adjusted free cash flow margin and launched over 430 new product capabilities in the fiscal year.
platforms.relevance: Independent analyst validation of Snowflake's AI consumption inflection and margin discipline is critical intelligence for clients deciding whether Snowflake's platform-expansion play into agentic workflows justifies renewed or expanded contract commitments.

platforms.title: Databricks Grows Over 65% YoY, Surpasses $5.4 Billion Revenue Run-Rate, Doubles Down on Lakebase and Genie
platforms.summary: Databricks crossed a $5.4 billion revenue run-rate in Q4 FY2025, delivering over 65% year-over-year growth, and completed investments exceeding $7 billion including roughly $5B equity and $2B debt. The company is accelerating Lakebase, a serverless Postgres database for AI agents, and Genie, its conversational AI assistant for data querying.
platforms.relevance: Databricks' sustained hyper-growth and cash-flow positivity validate the lakehouse architecture as a durable enterprise standard, directly informing platform selection and vendor-risk assessments for consulting clients.

platforms.title: Snowflake Launches Cortex Code and $200M OpenAI Partnership: New AI Tools Unveiled
platforms.summary: Snowflake unveiled a $200 million multi-year partnership with OpenAI, making OpenAI models natively available within its Cortex AI environment across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Alongside this, Snowflake launched Cortex Code, an AI coding agent that applies enterprise governance and security controls to accelerate pipeline and application development.
platforms.relevance: Natively embedding frontier LLMs inside a governed data platform removes a key adoption barrier for enterprise AI; consulting leaders should evaluate how this changes the competitive dynamics for clients currently routing OpenAI API calls outside their data perimeter.

planning.title: SAP Completes Acquisition of Prior Labs
planning.summary: SAP completed the acquisition of Prior Labs, a pioneer in Tabular Foundation Models, adding specialized AI capabilities for enterprise planning and decision-making.
planning.relevance: Demonstrates SAP's aggressive AI acquisition strategy to embed foundation models into planning and analytics; critical for competitive positioning against AI-native planning vendors.

planning.title: Anaplan Named Leader in 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Sales Performance Management
planning.summary: Anaplan scored the highest Ability to Execute among evaluated vendors in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Sales Performance Management, linking revenue performance management to financial, workforce, and supply chain planning on a single platform.
planning.relevance: Validates Anaplan's connected xP&A strategy and AI roadmap acceleration; reinforces enterprise platform positioning for connected planning across finance, operations, and revenue functions.

planning.title: SAP Completes Acquisition of Dremio
planning.summary: SAP completed its acquisition of Dremio, an open high-performance data lakehouse platform, expanding SAP's data infrastructure capabilities for enterprise analytics and planning workloads.
planning.relevance: Represents SAP's strategic consolidation of data platform assets to support Analytics Cloud and integrated planning, signaling competitive moves against data-native planning alternatives.

planning.title: EPM Software Trends 2026: What Gartner's Financial Planning Research Means for FP&A Leaders
planning.summary: Analysis of Gartner's December 2025 Magic Quadrant for Financial Planning Software shows industry pivot toward AI-assisted planning, xP&A, integrated business planning, and continuous planning capabilities, with xP&A extending FP&A discipline across operations, supply chain, and workforce.
planning.relevance: Synthesizes Gartner's authoritative view of 2026 EPM landscape: AI, xP&A, and cross-functional planning are now table-stakes; foundational data and process governance remain critical differentiators.

planning.title: Vibe Coding Is Coming to Finance. CFOs Need Guardrails (BCG)
planning.summary: BCG explores how AI coding agents enable finance teams to build custom FP&A forecasting and controllership applications without deep software engineering skills, while maintaining auditability and governance through rule-based code execution.
planning.relevance: Signals emerging pattern of AI-augmented low-code custom finance applications running alongside core EPM platforms; implications for architecture strategy and make-versus-buy decisions in enterprise planning stacks.

planning.title: The CFO's AI Agenda: From Automation to Advantage (BCG)
planning.summary: BCG research reveals the gap between CFO AI investment expectations and actual impact, with only 10% of AI success attributable to models themselves and 70% dependent on organizational readiness, governance, and people. Emphasizes domain-level transformation and workflow redesign as prerequisites for scaling AI.
planning.relevance: Exposes the implementation realities behind AI in planning: success depends on data quality, process standardization, and change management—not just platform capability—critical context for EPM platform selection and deployment.

planning.title: Finance Transformation Is Necessary. Here's How CFOs Can Make It Happen (BCG)
planning.summary: BCG framework for CFO-led transformations emphasizes defining clear objectives, pinpointing three priority changes, securing high-influence partners, delivering early wins, and embedding AI and analytics incrementally within live workflows rather than pursuing full platform overhauls.
planning.relevance: Practical roadmap for finance transformation that challenges monolithic platform migration approaches; validates incremental, outcome-driven deployment of planning and analytics capabilities aligned to business decision priorities.

planning.title: Pigment on the Path to $100M ARR: Launches AI Intent Modeling with Modeler Agent
planning.summary: Pigment announced it is approaching $100M in annual recurring revenue after doubling ARR for the third consecutive year, with 56% of new customers migrating from legacy vendors. The company launched its Modeler Agent, turning weeks-long planning model builds into hours or minutes through natural language intent modeling.
planning.relevance: Demonstrates how AI-native planning platforms are capturing market share from legacy EPM vendors, signaling the market's shift to agentic planning as a core competitive feature.

planning.title: ERP Modernization for AI: Transform Your Enterprise (McKinsey)
planning.summary: McKinsey research highlights the critical gap between AI agent development and ERP modernization, with high performers focusing on domain-level workflows rather than isolated use cases, working backward from specific business decisions to identify supporting ERP data, transactions, and rules.
planning.relevance: Essential strategic insight for data/analytics leaders: AI-driven planning requires aligned ERP infrastructure, data quality, and workflow redesign—planning platforms alone cannot deliver value without upstream systems transformation.

planning.title: AI in Finance: Driving Automation and Business Value (McKinsey)
planning.summary: McKinsey research found 44% of CFOs now use generative AI for over five use cases in 2025, up from 7% in the prior year, with decision support agents and agentic AI enabling real-time scenario planning and anomaly detection across finance workflows.
planning.relevance: Critical market validation of agentic AI adoption in finance; establishes the business case for AI-first planning platforms and finance transformation investments.

research.title: McKinsey Layoffs 2026: 10% Job Cuts Due to AI-Driven Productivity
research.summary: McKinsey is cutting 3,000-4,000 positions (~10% of workforce) in 2025-2026 as AI tools compress delivery timelines and reduce hours required for research and analysis. Cuts concentrate in back-office, junior research, and support roles where generative AI has achieved 40% productivity gains. Bain, BCG, Deloitte, and Accenture are implementing similar AI-driven staffing reductions.
research.relevance: Demonstrates how AI is reshaping consulting economics itself—signaling structural contraction in junior headcount, shift from time-based to outcome-based pricing, and pressure on traditional MBB business models.

research.title: The State of AI in the Enterprise 2026
research.summary: Deloitte's 2026 survey of 3,235 leaders finds worker AI access rose 50% in 2025, with companies expecting production project counts to double in six months. However, only 34% are reimagining the business; the AI skills gap is cited as the biggest integration barrier, with education (not role redesign) as companies' primary talent response.
research.relevance: Reveals the operational reality: enterprises have deployed AI broadly but struggle with transformation governance, talent readiness, and organizational change—core consulting demand.

research.title: Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026: Lakehouse Becomes the Agentic Enterprise Control Plane
research.summary: Bain analysis of Databricks 2026 summit shows enterprise AI is moving beyond agent demos into agent operations, with Lakehouse platforms evolving from data storage to agentic control planes. Key shifts include context-as-production-infrastructure, runtime governance enforcement, and live-truth-as-AI-infrastructure.
research.relevance: Identifies infrastructure and architectural inflection point where enterprise data platforms are becoming operational AI execution engines, creating new consulting demand around governance, orchestration, and real-time data.

research.title: Four Ways to Accelerate Growth with AI and Analytics
research.summary: BCG outlines how companies can use analytics and AI to shape growth strategy, mining customer data, patent networks, and emerging signals using agentic AI. The firm argues that companies not already using analytics to drive growth face significant competitive risk.
research.relevance: Demonstrates how top-tier consulting firms are reframing analytics from efficiency to growth, reshaping the strategic value proposition and client engagement models in 2026.

research.title: Scaling agentic AI with data transformations
research.summary: McKinsey reports that data limitations are cited by 80% of companies as a roadblock to scaling agentic AI, requiring modernized data architectures, quality enforcement, and evolved operating models. The article recommends unified data foundations, security-by-default governance, and continuous performance visibility.
research.relevance: Critical for data & analytics leaders planning infrastructure investments; identifies why most agentic AI deployments stall and the foundational data strategy required for consulting client success.

research.title: Gartner Top Predictions for Data and Analytics 2026
research.summary: Gartner warns that 50% of AI agent deployment failures by 2030 will stem from insufficient governance platform runtime enforcement. The firm recommends D&A leaders experiment with data governance agents in low-risk pipelines and redesign analytic workflows to include mandatory evaluation stages.
research.relevance: Identifies the emerging governance gap in agent-centric enterprises and signals where data & analytics consulting practices must evolve to capture value.

research.title: Private Equity's Future: Digital First and AI Powered
research.summary: BCG research shows PE teams are channeling digital efforts toward decision support, process automation, and commercial excellence, treating digital as core to AI. ERP and CRM systems are now prioritized as AI-ready data foundations, with firms evaluating vendors on API architectures and embedded AI readiness.
research.relevance: Signals massive enterprise demand for data strategy and AI-ready systems architecture consulting, with PE sponsors treating these as value-creation levers.

research.title: Why the McKinsey Layoffs Signal a Reckoning for Consulting in the AI Age
research.summary: Analysis argues McKinsey's 10% workforce reduction signals an irreversible shift in consulting value creation. As AI democratizes access to information and analytical capability, the traditional information-asymmetry advantage of strategy firms is eroding. The premium for future consulting talent will shift from analytical horsepower to judgment, client relationships, and execution capability.
research.relevance: Critical for understanding how the consulting and analytics business itself is being reshaped by AI—consulting leaders must adapt pricing models, team structures, and value propositions or risk obsolescence.

research.title: Why AI Stumbles Without a Solid Data Strategy
research.summary: Bain's cross-industry research shows that AI at scale requires broader, more robust governance jointly managed by business and data technology teams. Case study of a North American utility demonstrates how data maturity mapping and governance operationalization delivered 20-25% efficiency gains and $10 million in recovered value.
research.relevance: Shows why data and analytics consulting remains mission-critical; enterprises cannot move from AI pilots to production scale without fundamental data governance transformation.

research.title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
research.summary: McKinsey's latest survey of 1,993 executives across 105 countries reveals that AI high performers are treating agents as critical transformational tools, with 38% of respondents from companies earning over $1 billion annually. Nearly two-thirds of enterprises have experimented with agents, but fewer than 10% have successfully scaled them to deliver tangible value.
research.relevance: Essential baseline for understanding how global enterprise leaders assess AI maturity, agent deployment, and the gap between experimentation and productive scale—directly shaping consulting demand.
